construction.primitive_kat: test/vectors/algorithm-suite.json -- row 1 selects the primitive, row 3 the composition
construction.kdf: HKDF-SHA256 via WebCrypto deriveBits, at open
construction.store_aad: LP("done/store/v1") || LP(principal_id) || LP(workspace_id) || LP(store_id) || LP(dec v) || LP(dec gen) || LP(dec seq) || LP(kind)
construction.envelope_aad: LP("done/keyenv/v1") || LP(principal_id) || LP(workspace_id) || LP(dec v) || LP(dec gen) || LP(purpose)
construction.length_prefix: uint16be(byteLength) || utf8 -- injective, so no field can shift another
construction.stored_record: { v, gen, seq, kind, nonce[12], ct } as a structured clone; ct carries the 16-byte tag
construction.key_envelope: { v, gen, nonce[12], ct } as a structured clone; ct carries the 16-byte tag
construction.nonce: 12 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues() per record, under a 2^32-per-(store, generation) budget counted by the SeqCounter's reserved[gen] -- reserved before encryption, so an abandoned invocation is counted; never read from seq (P-3, S0-3)
construction.store_id: minted from local randomness at store creation beside the SeqCounter it names; one key per counter, so the nonce budget binds the key it protects for every device count
construction.nonce_caveat: Nonces are fixed inputs in these vectors so the composition is testable. Production generates them randomly; the fixed nonce is not the discipline.
construction.l_local_caveat: L_local is raw bytes here because a vector needs bytes. In production it is a structured-cloned non-extractable CryptoKey with no extractable representation (§13.3).

vectors.name: update-record
vectors.why: The common case: one keystroke-sized Yjs update under the first generation.

vectors.name: state-record
vectors.why: Same store, same generation, kind=state. Proves kind is bound: a state record supersedes every record before it, so a record whose kind can be edited can delete the store.

vectors.name: empty-update
vectors.why: A zero-length plaintext still authenticates; framing and tag must not depend on payload length.

vectors.name: rotated-generation
vectors.why: A different K_g, so a different K_store. The cleartext gen is what selects which; it is in the AAD, so it cannot be edited to point at a generation the record was not sealed under.

vectors.name: second-workspace
vectors.why: Same K_g, same nonce, same plaintext, different workspace. Proves the subkey is workspace-bound by derivation, not only by AAD.

vectors.name: second-store
vectors.why: Same K_g, same workspace, same nonce, same plaintext, different store id. Proves the subkey is store-bound by derivation, not only by AAD — one key per SeqCounter, so no per-store comparison can undercount a shared key (P-3 falsifier 14).

envelopes.name: key-envelope
envelopes.why: K_g sealed under L_local. This is what the key store holds and what §6.1 opens before anything else; every content record above is unreadable until this one opens.

envelopes.name: key-envelope-rotated
envelopes.why: The second generation, sealed under the same L_local. A device holds one envelope per generation its records still use (§6.1, §13.7).

must_fail.name: wrong-workspace-subkey
must_fail.mutate: Derive K_store for a different workspace id.

must_fail.name: wrong-store-subkey
must_fail.mutate: Derive K_store for a different store id, workspace unchanged. The wrong-store sibling of wrong-workspace-subkey: two stores holding one K_g never derive one subkey, so a record sealed for one store fails to open under the key of another (P-3 falsifier 14).

must_fail.name: wrong-principal
must_fail.mutate: Authenticate with a different principal in the AAD.

must_fail.name: wrong-workspace-aad
must_fail.mutate: Authenticate with a different workspace in the AAD, subkey unchanged.

must_fail.name: wrong-generation
must_fail.mutate: Claim gen=2 in the AAD for a record sealed under gen=1.

must_fail.name: kind-swapped
must_fail.mutate: Reinterpret an update record as a state record.

must_fail.name: seq-edited
must_fail.mutate: Renumber seq from 1 to 99 to reorder the trim.

must_fail.name: version-downgraded
must_fail.mutate: Renumber v from 1 to 0 to select a suite this reader does not have.

must_fail.name: flipped-tag-bit
must_fail.mutate: Flip the low bit of the final tag byte.

must_fail.name: truncated-ciphertext
must_fail.mutate: Drop the final byte of ct.

must_fail.name: envelope-aad-on-record
must_fail.mutate: Open a content record with a key-envelope AAD.

must_fail.name: record-aad-on-envelope
must_fail.mutate: Open a key envelope with a content-record AAD.

must_fail.name: record-aad-only-label
must_fail.mutate: Authenticate a content record with the key-envelope label, every record field unchanged. Isolates the labels contribution from the field difference the whole-AAD swaps also carry.

must_fail.name: record-aad-only-store
must_fail.mutate: Authenticate a content record claiming the other store id in the AAD, subkey unchanged. Isolates the AAD binding from the derivation binding wrong-store-subkey carries.

must_fail.name: envelope-aad-only-label
must_fail.mutate: Authenticate a key envelope with the content-record label, every envelope field unchanged.

must_fail.name: envelope-aad-only-principal
must_fail.mutate: A key envelope claiming the other principal on the same profile (PRD §6.7s ordinary case).

must_fail.name: envelope-aad-only-workspace
must_fail.mutate: A key envelope claiming the other workspace. L_local is a device key, not a workspace key, so nothing but the AAD separates the two slots.

must_fail.name: envelope-aad-only-version
must_fail.mutate: A key envelope renumbered to v=0. The carrier version selects the whole suite (row 1), so it must fail to open rather than select a weaker one.

must_fail.name: envelope-aad-only-generation
must_fail.mutate: A gen=1 envelope claiming gen=2, which is how a superseded content key would be made to look current.

must_fail.name: envelope-aad-only-purpose
must_fail.mutate: A content-key envelope opened as a device-signing-key envelope. This is the substitution purpose exists to prevent, and nothing tested it.
